assertions.rationale: A raw prose fragment from the review-history narrative. A meaning-preserving edit (`no High or Critical findings`, `without Critical or High findings`) leaves the fact intact and breaks the assertion, which is the defining C failure mode.

assertions.rationale: A mid-sentence prose fragment of the section 12 approval narrative. `accepted and amended findings` preserves the meaning and breaks the check; the durable contract is that the Fable 5 adjudication was incorporated, not this exact wording.

assertions.contract_summary: Section 12 records that the "rejected F-004 consolidation was not applied".
assertions.rationale: A prose clause that happens to name F-004. The finding ID alone would be a structural token, but the assertion pins the whole clause, so any reword of the surrounding sentence (`the F-004 consolidation, which was rejected, was not applied`) breaks it while preserving the meaning.

assertions.contract_summary: Section 12 opens with the sentence prefix "Version 1.4 is approved as a maintenance update".
assertions.rationale: A prose sentence prefix, not the `**Version:**` field. This repository already classifies Version-in-prose as C (`The intro states \`Version 1.7 is now the most recent **Approved**\` baseline`) and Version-as-field as D; this is the prose form, and `Version 1.4 is approved as a maintenance release` would preserve the meaning while breaking it.

assertions.contract_summary: Section 12 records that the user "answered 「ok」 to the complete decision brief".
assertions.rationale: The user original 「ok」 is D-grade evidence, but the assertion literal wraps it in author-written prose (`answered ... to the complete decision brief`). The repository already draws this line: a bare verbatim quote is D (DECISIONS.md SD-025's 「ok」), a quote bundled with an author-written wrapper is C (the UI_SPEC.md acceptance-quote entries). Rewording the wrapper preserves the acceptance fact and breaks this check, so the wrapper -- not the quote -- sets the category.
